subject: geography

provenance.source: AglaSem Docs copy of the NTA master question paper (CUET UG 2026 Question Paper Geography and Geology, 41 PDF pages: a cover plus 40 numbered pages), https://docs.aglasem.com/view/7025c4b2-c701-11f1-a920-0aa932765c8b, PDF https://cdn.aglasem.com/aglasem-doc/7025c4b2-c701-11f1-a920-0aa932765c8b/7025c4b2-c701-11f1-a920-0aa932765c8b.pdf (9,253,417 bytes, ETag a10882e42d56b568fdf01186f7b5c693, Last-Modified 13 Oct 2026), downloaded 22 Nov 2026 under the owner's 22 Nov 2026 request for more subjects. English text from two OCR drafts (Windows OCR and RapidOCR) cross-checked against each other and the page images. Answers from NTA's CUET (UG) 2026 final answer key (option ids), subject 313.
provenance.keySource: A question is authenticated when its printed NTA question id is in the 24-05-2026 (Second) final key for subject 313 and the key option id is one of its four printed option ids. Printed option ids are consecutive per question.

bankRead: One read-only read on 22 Nov 2026 with the repo read script (SELECT only): 223 visible geography rows, of which 214 pass readablePracticeQuestions (equals the 214 in the 21 Nov inventory snapshot; the 9 others are visible but not eligible and are not cited). Served copy: tmp/1122-coverage/snap/geography/served_rows.json and served_geography.json (eligibility output eligible.txt).
keyCardDeck: data/keycards/decks/geography.json (v3, 1345 cards; key_card_suspended was not re-read, the earlier subjects had none suspended)
syllabusSource: Bank and deck chapter names for geography (Fundamentals of Human Geography and India: People and Economy); every question sits on the 2026 syllabus. Chapter labels for items 18 and 22 are best guesses where the bank has no home for the fact.
method: data/coverage/METHOD.md (STRICT rule; doubtful = not covered; Key cards count for theory; an answer readable off a printed passage is skill). Facts written first: tmp/1122-coverage/checkerA-geo/A_facts_before_search.txt. Search: tmp/1122-coverage/checkerA-geo/s.mjs over the served copy and the deck; builder build_A.mjs checks every cited id.
paperStructure: One compulsory Geography paper of 50 questions: Sub-section 1 = 40 single questions (Q51-90: one-line MCQs, 5 sequence, 5 statement, 5 match), Sub-section 2 = a passage on high-technology industry with 5 questions (Q91-95), Sub-section 3 = a passage on rail transport with 5 questions (Q96-100). The printed header says 42 questions; fifty ids are printed and the key has 50 rows for this shift.

facts: Push factors of migration include unemployment (also poor living conditions, political turmoil, natural disasters); pull factors are better jobs, peace, pleasant climate

matches.teaches: push factors: unemployment, poor living conditions, political turmoil, unpleasant climate, disasters, epidemics
push factors are conditions at the origin; conditions at the destination are pull factors

questions.reason: Key card lists unemployment as a push factor; the bank row says the destination-side conditions are pull factors, so the other three options are ruled out.

facts: The Radical school of thought applied Marxian theory to explain poverty, deprivation and social inequality

matches.teaches: Radical school employed Marxian theory to explain poverty, deprivation and social inequality

questions.chapter: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
facts: Natural wastelands: gullied land, desertic sands, barren rocky areas, steep slopes, glacial areas; human-caused: degraded plantation land, forests, pastures, mining and industrial wastelands

matches.teaches: barren rocky areas and steep sloping land are wastelands caused by natural agents
degraded plantation land, forests, pastures, mining and industrial wastelands are caused by human action

questions.reason: The two cards split the types, so barren rocky and steep land is the one not caused by human action.

facts: WTO rules do not cover worker rights and child labour; they cover trade rules, services and intellectual property
questions.reason: Cards say the WTO covers trade rules, services and intellectual rights, and that it has been criticised; nothing says worker rights or child labour are left out.

facts: Pipelines carry milk from farms to factories in New Zealand
